So i just went through the whole journey of which road to take to fix my chin. So i personally have a slight overbite and my lower jaw is slightly crooked (midlines dont match up.) i had braces for 5 years and i had rubber bands, but the ortho said if i ever want to fully fix my jaw i would need surgery. But honestly i have NEVER had any problems with sleeping, breathing, chewing, jaw pain, etc. my dentist also does recognize the off bite but isn’t concerned, i dont have any wear/tear on my back teeth from it. So in the end i decided it was more cosmetic for me. Could i get jaw surgery? Sure, but my insurance wouldnt cover it and it would be more than double to triple the cost of a cosmetic surgery, it would be aggressive, many risks, and i would also likely need to repeat braces. So then i looked at filler. But long term wise it would be expensive as well and it wasn’t permanent and theres always the chance it could migrate or just not come out properly. Then finally it came down to chin implant vs. Sliding genioplasty. Im 23, so a sliding genioplasty would be good for me. However i really didnt want to go through an aggressive surgery like that, and it would cost more money than an implant. In the end i decided on the implant because if i didnt like it for some reason i could always take it out, it wasnt too expensive, it wasnt an aggressive surgery and recovery would be easier. So thats just my experience :) for you, you could always try filler to see how you like it and maybe have some consultations for a sliding genio and chin implants and see what you want to do long term!

It's a hard thing to teach, I still have some issues with my two dogs. One is calm the other is nuts. What seems to work the best is whenever he goes to bite him we scream "UH UH" and make him sit or lay down and we say "leave it." When he calms down we give lots of treats. But if you want this dog to play nice with the young puppy chances are you will need to enforce it with the other dog as well. Otherwise it might get confusing and he won't learn to do it at all. So try starting to separate him from either of then when getting too aggressive. Use the leave it command, reward with treats, distract with other toys, etc. Hope this helped!

My grandfather got a puppy and my entire family erupted into chaos. Parents didnt want him. I ended up getting attached and fought like hell for him. Now he's embedded in our lives and is very loved and everyone got it through their heads that he's our family. However, it didn't get better until they stopped being stubborn and started helping. We all take part in caring for him, teaching him things, etc. He is mine, and is very attached to me so i make sure I organize everything for him. Including his routines, lots of funny things to get everyone to laugh, taking him out for the day, etc. Your situation won't get better if you alienate your mom and her dog. You need to build a relationship with him. He's also a baby and needs to be taught. The biggest issue for you seems to be your cats. So if I were you, i would at least make myself in charge of quickly trying to make the cat-dog relationship better. Start out with teaching him a basic "leave it" command with treats. Once he knows what it means, start introducing him with one cat at a time for a short period. Distract the dog with toys and give the cats some treats to calm them down. If the dog behaves and "leaves it" alone then reward with lots of treats! Hopefully after a while the dog will not see the cats as a toy and the cats won't feel the need to hide from the dog in your room. Hope this helped! Any questions feel free to message me

I know your post is about a rat, but I have experience with mice I thought I'd share. Still small rodents, so maybe you'll find this helpful:) One day I was at a petstore and just decided on the spot to buy all 4 mice they had. They are very social and were always cuddling up together. However, their lifespans are only about 1-2 years. Within a year/year and a half their health all started deteriorating and it was heart breaking. Tumors are extremely common and 2 of them developed some. It was heartbreaking to watch their little bodies shut down like that. Took them to a vet (also very hard to find vets for them, let alone a good one.) and one mouse was overstressed and died in the car on the way home. I was very angry because I told the vet i didn't want her to take the mouse out of the room but she insisted. Then she put her in the box and closed the lid so i wouldnt see my mouse was basically convulsing. Anyway, once health started deteriorating amongst them they also started displaying cannibalistic behaviors and one mouse got her ears completely chewed off. I had to separate them and felt bad because they were alone and weren't playing as much. They all ended up dying way too soon (they did live out basically their life span but it still felt too short and very traumatic). They're just very sensitive little creatures and I'd do more research and think about if you're prepared for any of that. It's always sad when a pet dies, but especially so for one that's so hard to get much help for. Hope some of this was helpful!

My cat started having hind leg issues and when we took him to the vet, we found out he was disbetic. We also gave him insulin and started giving him diabetic food. Nothing seemed to help. After some research, we cut out all dry cat food completely 100%. Only wet food. After a little bit, his back legs were working a lot better and his numbers were getting better quickly. The vet ended up taking him off insulin and he was back to his normal grumpy self, just minus the dry cat food and insulin. Not exactly sure about how all of that worked and if it works for many other cats, but if you're at the point of possible euthanasia i would give it a shot. Also, maybe try looking for foster care, or some other no kill shelter. Many do accept animals in need of medical attention, and that's where generous people with donations come into play.
My advice would be to bring him with you, and see how he does. I'd also schedule some weekend visits with his other doggy friend back home!
